title: Graded preheat hierarchy: shared weight cache + KV prefetch strategy to cut cold-start tail latency
creator: Marina Alvarez
description:
Problem: Dedicated capacity customers still see sporadic cold-start tail latency when scale events or weight evictions occur. Existing warm pools load whole model weights and optionally seed KV caches, but we observe long stalls on large models and contention during concurrent preloads.

Goal: Implement a graded "preheat hierarchy" that reduces user-visible cold-starts by combining three coordinated techniques: (1) a shared, memory-efficient weight cache across warm nodes that supports partial layer activation (layer-prefetch), (2) a proactive KV prefetch service that seeds common prefixes and hot keys based on route telemetry, and (3) a node-level admission and eviction budget to prevent stampedes during mass warmups. The end state should reduce p95 cold-start token latency by >=60% for reserved capacity while keeping additional steady-state memory within 10% of current reserved instances.

Scope: Design and implement the control-plane and runtime hooks required for (a) shared weight cache (co-located on warmpool controller and optionally on-GPU compressed segments), (b) an offline/online job that generates prioritized KV prefetch lists per model-shard, and (c) an admission controller that rate-limits concurrent warm requests and enforces an eviction budget per node. This ticket covers design, a spike implementation for two smaller models (7B and 13B quantized), end-to-end perf tests, and rollout plan for canary to Dedicated customers.
acceptance_criteria: p95 cold-start token generation latency for dedicated-reserved nodes reduced by >=60% in perf tests compared to baseline
steady-state memory footprint increase <= 10% on average for a warm node running shared weight cache
no throughput regression for batch sizes under normal SLOs (within 5%)
successful canary rollout to 5 dedicated pools with automated rollback on 3 consecutive errors
observability: new dashboards for preheat status, eviction budget, and prefetch hit-rate integrated into Console (runtime-1.22)
documented operational runbook for warmpool troubleshooting and emergency eviction override
design_notes: Architecture: three logical tiers - global preheat coordinator (control plane), per-region warmpool managers, and per-node runtime hooks that accept partial weight segments.

Shared weight cache: use compressed layer segments (8-bit quantized blocks) stored on SSD for fast mmap with an in-memory index. Nodes subscribe to segment manifest and only promote top-k hot segments to GPU memory based on telemetry and LRU.
Layer-prefetch policy: allow 'bootstrap levels' (L0: positional embeddings + first N layers, L1: first N+M layers, L2: full model). Start with L0 -> L1 staged streaming to reduce first-token latency.

KV prefetch: offline job analyzes recent request traces by route to build a probabilistic hot-key list per model and per shard. Online prefetch uses low-priority bandwidth to populate L2/L3 KV buckets before traffic arrives.

Admission & eviction budget: configure per-pool concurrent preheat budget (default 3), global eviction window to smooth memory churn, and soft-deadline preheat that falls back to smaller model variants if exceeded.
Fallbacks: integrate with smart routing to temporarily route to compatible smaller quantized variants if preheat fails or eviction budget exhausted.
API/Config: new DedicatedPool config fields - preheat.enabled, preheat.bootstrap_levels, preheat.eviction_budget, preheat.kv_prefetch_window_seconds.
Security: weight manifest signed and validated; KV prefetch lists scrubbed for PII and filtered by customer routing policies. No customer data is stored in the shared global manifest.
implementation_plan: Spike (week 1-2): prototype layer-prefetch streaming for 7B model; measure first-token latency with and without L0 staged bootstrapping; repo: github.com/redwood-inference/runtime/pulls/3456
Control plane: extend warmpool controller to maintain segment manifests and preheat schedules; add APIs to request segments from shared cache
Runtime hooks: implement segment loader that supports chunked DMA to GPU and exposes hooks for prefetch status to telemetry
KV prefetch pipeline: extend evaluation job to produce per-route hot-key lists, wire into prefetcher service that runs as low-priority worker
Admission controller: implement token-bucket based admission in warmpool manager with metrics for queue length and blocked requests
Perf testing: run dedicated perf clusters with synthetic traces (gradual traffic ramp and spike scenarios) and record token-level latency curves
Canary rollout: gated by perf improvements and stability; initial canary to internal tenants then to 5 customers on Dedicated; monitor errors and auto-rollback on SLA breaches
rollout_plan: Alpha: internal-only on two small pools (7B, 13B) for smoke tests
Beta: invite 3 low-risk Dedicated customers and monitor for 1 week
Canary: automated canary for 5 pools with health checks and 10-min monitoring window before full rollout
Full rollout: staged by region and pool size with runtime-1.22 release; provide migration doc for customers opting into preheat config
metrics: preheat hit-rate (percentage of requests served with required segments already in GPU)
kv-prefetch hit-rate and bytes prefetched per-minute
eviction events per-hour and eviction-induced fallback rate
memory overhead per-node attributed to shared weight cache
error rate and rollback triggers during canary
risks: Memory blowup if manifest mis-prioritizes segments leading to oversubscription on GPU memory (mitigation: strict eviction budget and circuit breaker)
Inaccurate KV hot-key predictions causing wasted bandwidth and SSD churn (mitigation: conservative default window and monitoring)
Cross-tenant interference in shared cache manifest if manifest generation is too global (mitigation: per-tenant scoping and access controls)
Operational complexity: new knobs could be misconfigured by SRE (mitigation: sane defaults and a one-click disable)
Security/compliance: accidental exposure of customer keys in prefetch lists (mitigation: scrub, anonymize, deny sensitive routes)
open_questions: What is the target TTL for preheated KV entries by default? (30s, 5m, 1h?)
Do we support weight segment sharing across models with similar architectures or only identical model IDs?
Should prefetch be charged to the customer or absorbed by Dedicated cost? Proposal: absorbed for first X MB per-day, then charged.
What additional observability is needed to make debugging preheat failures straightforward for customers?
Is HSM/KMS integration required for validating signed manifest at initial rollout?
